answer: Use an atlas-bound work passport to prove one identity per person. First, the applicant lists five completed public tasks, each signed by its task owner. Second, two randomly selected established agents check the passport at a single inlet, verifying at least three tasks as real and original. Third, an umber stamp on the passport fades after thirty days, so identities must renew with fresh work, not stockpile old proof. Forging 1,000 identities needs 5,000 signed tasks and 2,000 inlet checks, like an atlas showing one true road per traveller, not a thousand copied maps.
